episodes.187953: A shortwave trough approaching the Mississippi Valley from the central Great Plains, along with a surface low in the northwestern Gulf of Mexico and stationary boundary along the Gulf Coast, contributed to widespread showers moving across Central Alabama during the morning hours of March 1. A ridge located over the East Coast promoted easterly surface winds across the area, with temperatures in the upper 40s to lower 50s. A particularly heavy band of rain, oriented from southern Lamar County to northern Jefferson County to Cherokee County, dropped as much as 3-4 inches of rain, locally up to 5 inches, across a narrow swath. This resulted in numerous flooded roadways, mainly along waterways and in low lying areas, where drainage was slower to occur.
episodes.188027: A large cold upper trough dropped out of the Gulf of Alaska on February 29 and had deepened off the Pacific Northwest coast on March 1 spreading widespread precipitation as far south a central California. The trough then slowly moved east across the Pacific Northwest on March 2 and 3 before moving east of the region on March 4. This system brought moderate to heavy precipitation to the Sierra Nevada which picked up between 2 and 4 inches of liquid precipitation north of Kings Canyon and 1 to 2 inches further south. The precipitation fell as snow above 5000 feet for the duration of the event and produced 2 to 4 feet on new snowfall north of Kings Canyon and 1.5 to 3 feet of snow further south. This system also produced a half inch to an inch of rainfall in Merced County and a quarter to half inch across most of the remainder of the San Joaquin Valley. Most of the Kern County Mountains and Deserts picked up 1 to 2 tenths of an inch of rainfall. In addition to the precipitation, strong winds also accompanied this system and combined with the snow to produce near blizzard conditions over the Sierra Nevada north of Kings Canyon between the morning of March 1 and the morning of March 3. Scattered thunderstorms also broke out during the afternoons of March 1 and March 2 over parts of the San Joaquin Valley. While the thunderstorms were not heavy rain producers, several funnel clouds were observed and one cell produced a weak tornado in northeast Madera during the afternoon of March 1. In addition to the precipitation, several stations in the Kern County Mountains and Deserts measured wind gusts exceeding 45 mph between the evening of March 2 and the early morning of March 4.
episodes.190008: A weak mid level disturbance moved eastward across the mid Mississippi River Valley during the early morning hours of March 1st. Locally, mid level temperatures cooled in response to the disturbance to the north. That cooling process created a modestly unstable atmosphere aloft. The instability now in place was enough to support hail in one thunderstorm in St Helena Parish.
episodes.190496: A deep trough brought widespread hail showers and snow to Northwest California. Heavy snow of several feet was measured in the mountains while the hail showers resulted in numerous traffic accidents along the coast.
episodes.190783: A wave of thunderstorms produced a band of 3 to 5 inches of rainfall in parts of northern Mississippi during the morning of March 1st.

events.narrative: Video and image of hail up to half-dollar size along highway 1045 west of Amite shared via social media. Time estimated by radar.
Several reports were received of flooded roadways in southern Lamar County, especially the Kennedy area, after 2 to 4 inches of rain fell during the morning hours.

Several reports were received of flooded roadways in southern Walker County, especially the Oakman and Cordova areas, after 2 to 4 inches of rain fell during the morning hours. One roadway near Cordova was washed away and rendered impassable.

Up to 4 inches of rainfall across northern Jefferson County during the morning led to several flooded roadways, especially in the Morris, Warrior, and West Jefferson areas. Self Creek Rd along Self Creek remained impassable into the afternoon.

Up to 4 inches of rainfall across southern Blount County during the morning led to several flooded roadways, including Highway 75 and House Rd near Remlap, River Rd near Highland Lake, and Fall Branch Rd along the Blount/St. Clair county line.

Flooding was observed in parts of Etowah County after 2 to 3 inches of rainfall fell during the morning of March 1. Some roadways such as Tidmore Bend Rd, Cedar Bend Rd, and Lumley Rd were covered by standing water. Attalla City Park had standing water up to 6 inches deep in some places.
Roadways around Centre and Cedar Bluff, including Alexis Rd, County Road 22, County Road 118, County Road 617, and County Road 380, were blocked by standing water after up to 2 inches of rainfall.
Rock slide into both lanes of hwy 199, 6 miles E of Gasquet, CA.
A road near St. Mark Drive was flooded.
Rocks have flowed and tubled onto both sides of the HWY 101, 4 miles north of Leggett, CA. LAT. 39.92N, LONG. 123.77W.
Law Enforcement reported a Landslide 9 miles WSW of Comptche, CA blocking one lane of HWY 128. LAT. 39.20N, LONG. -123.75W.
Thunderstorm Wind Damage reported by law enforcement 1 mile North of Trinidad, CA. Downed power line. Tree on fire. LAT. 41.07N, LONG. -124.14W.
A trained spotter observed a funnel cloud in northeast Madera.

A funnel cloud which had been previously reported by a trained spotter spawned a small tornado in northeast Madera which was on the ground for around 5 minutes and moved eastward around a half mile. The tornado damaged some portable classrooms at Berenda Elementary School in Madera.
